text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; since you are a newborn presenting with seizures and lethargy three days after birth, I need to ask: Was your mother diabetic, and did you have any trouble breathing or feeding immediately after delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a 31-week preterm infant with chorioamnionitis, poor Apgar scores, and late-onset seizures is highly suspicious for sepsis and hypoxic-ischemic injury. Did your baby experience any episodes of cyanosis or apnea in the first 24 hours of life? REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture, CBC, and CRP.
